title: Buildings and getting things done in town
intro: Places you need and the words for dealing with them. See unit 8 for the street layout itself.

entries.note: el piso or el departamento is a flat; el apartamento too.
el apartamento and el piso (Spain) mean the same thing.

ex.es: Trabaja en el departamento de ventas.
ex.en: He works in the sales department.

entries.note: la colonia in Mexico. el vecino is the neighbour — see unit 3.

ex.es: Es un barrio tranquilo y seguro.

entries.note: la salida is the exit, printed on every sign.

ex.es: Llama a la puerta antes de entrar.
ex.en: Knock on the door before going in.

ex.es: La entrada es por el otro lado.
ex.en: The entrance is on the other side.

entries.note: el elevador in Mexico. la escalera is the stairs — see unit 19.

ex.es: El ascensor está fuera de servicio.
ex.en: The lift is out of order.

ex.es: El techo tiene una mancha de humedad.
ex.en: The ceiling has a damp patch.

entries.note: rentar in Mexico, alquilar in Spain and much of South America. la renta or el alquiler is the rent.

ex.es: Alquilamos un carro por tres días.
ex.en: We rented a car for three days.

entries.note: el cuarto also means a room; la habitación is the hotel word.

ex.es: El hotel está lleno esta semana.
ex.en: The hotel is full this week.

entries.note: la reserva or la reservación is the booking.
The two words on every shop door, and the past participles of abrir and cerrar.
A common landmark in directions: en el semáforo, gira a la derecha.
hacer puente is to take the bridging day off between a holiday and the weekend.

ex.en: We crossed the bridge on foot.
Monday is part of a long weekend.

entries.note: el tránsito is preferred in much of South America. el atasco or el trancón is a traffic jam.

ex.en: I was late because of the traffic.

entries.note: estacionar in Latin America, aparcar in Spain. el estacionamiento is the car park.
la gasolinera is the petrol station; la nafta in Argentina.
See unit 8. Together they make up almost all spoken directions.

ex.es: Pegaron carteles por toda la calle.
ex.en: They put posters up all along the street.

entries.note: See unit 19 for la basura itself.

ex.en: The bin man comes on Tuesdays.

entries.note: See unit 23. Paired here because they are what you notice most about a neighbourhood.

ex.es: No soporto el ruido de la calle.
ex.en: I can't stand the street noise.

entries.note: See unit 34 for el seguro, insurance.

ex.es: Es una zona segura de noche.
ex.en: It's a safe area at night.
